svg.title: Ergodic regularity dichotomy in the original topology
svg.desc: The largest Radon part is invariant modulo null sets. Ergodicity forces either full Radon regularity or, inside every positive Borel set, a positive Borel remainder with no positive compact subset. Existence of the second branch under the full standard-measure source hypotheses remains open.

g.text: Which compact-extraction branch is possible?
Finite Borel measure · nonsingular homeomorphisms · ergodic measure-algebra action
Select the largest Radon part R modulo null sets — Proposition 3.8
A is a Radon part ⇔ every Borel E ⊂ A has compact inner approximation.
Countable unions of parts remain parts; their supremal mass is attained by one Borel R.
Transport gives μ(gR △ R) = 0 for every g. Ergodicity: μ(R) = 0 or μ(R) = μ(X).
R is conull: μ is Radon
Every positive Borel E contains a positive
compact subset in the original topology.
Pointwise freeness gives compact L ⊂ E
with μ(L) > 0 and gL ∩ L = ∅ for fixed g ≠ e.
One positive Radon part already forces
this branch. Theorem 3.10 / Corollary 3.11
R is null: no positive Radon part
Inside every positive E, choose H ⊂ E with
r(H) = sup μ(C), compact C ⊂ H, < μ(H).
Choose compact Dₙ ↑, μ(Dₙ) → r(H).
F = H ∖ ⋃ₙDₙ; μ(F) = μ(H) − r(H) > 0.
Compact C ⊂ F: μ(C) + μ(Dₙ) ≤ r(H),
so μ(C) = 0. Lemma 3.7 / Theorem 3.10
The second branch still gives measurable wandering sets — Corollary 3.12
For every compact K ⊂ G ∖ {e}, Theorem 3.2 extracts a positive Borel F′ ⊂ F:
F′ ∩ kF′ = ∅ for all k ∈ K, and every compact C ⊂ F′ is null.
The conull standard point-space premise forces this possible obstruction to be atomless.
Open source decision: do all standing hypotheses force the left branch?
This is a proved dichotomy; existence of the right branch at that full scope is not asserted.
Proof: Borel carriers and uniform wandering neighborhoods, Lemmas 3.7/3.9, Proposition 3.8, Theorem 3.10.
